evidence.claim: Article 69 makes the president head of state and guarantor of the constitution; Article 83 makes the president supreme commander of the armed forces; Article 85 allows proclamation of a state of urgency or state of siege after coordination with the prime minister and the chamber heads.
evidence.title: Congo (Democratic Republic of the) 2005 (rev. 2011)
evidence.excerpt: Article 69 makes the president head of state and guarantor of the constitution; Article 83 makes the president supreme commander of the armed forces; Article 85 allows proclamation of a state of urgency or state of siege after coordination with the prime minister and the chamber heads.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Text of the constitutional framework, directly relevant to office authority and emergency powers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Formal authority available to Tshisekedi in 2022, but not evidence of how he exercised it.
contrary_evidence: This is formal power, not proof of practical control or nuclear capability.

evidence.claim: Freedom House says the DRC's political system is paralyzed by manipulation of the electoral process by political elites, and that opposition parties and civil society frequently criticize CENI and the Constitutional Court for lacking independence.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House says the DRC's political system is paralyzed by manipulation of the electoral process by political elites, and that opposition parties and civil society frequently criticize CENI and the Constitutional Court for lacking independence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with explicit electoral-process and institutional-independence findings relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural under Tshisekedi's administration, though not all defects are personally ordered by him.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes some opposition members were released and some exiles returned under Tshisekedi.

evidence.claim: Freedom House reports that in August 2022 opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund, formerly an ally of President Tshisekedi, was arrested for allegedly insulting the president after launching a new opposition party in July.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House reports that in August 2022 opposition leader Jean-Marc Kabund, formerly an ally of President Tshisekedi, was arrested for allegedly insulting the president after launching a new opposition party in July.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent country report with a dated 2022 arrest tied to opposition activity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi-era treatment of a breakaway opposition figure.
contrary_evidence: The report does not by itself prove a presidential order; it documents the arrest as a political event.

evidence.claim: RSF says the national broadcaster RTNC lacks independence, local authorities commonly pressure journalists and media outlets, and the press law is obsolete and oppressive with prisons terms still attached to press offences.
evidence.title: République démocratique du Congo 2022 - EN
evidence.excerpt: RSF says the national broadcaster RTNC lacks independence, local authorities commonly pressure journalists and media outlets, and the press law is obsolete and oppressive with prisons terms still attached to press offences.
evidence.source_locator: Media landscape, political context, and legal framework sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent press-freedom monitor with direct country-level assessment of media control and legal pressure.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 media environment and inherited legal framework
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to the Tshisekedi administration's media environment and tolerance of independent information.
contrary_evidence: RSF also notes the authorities had committed to overhaul the press law, so the record includes stated reform intent.

evidence.claim: HRW says the military and police curtailed freedom of expression, used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and political opposition members under martial law in North Kivu and Ituri.
evidence.title: DR Congo: Martial Law Brings Crackdown in East
evidence.excerpt: HRW says the military and police curtailed freedom of expression, used lethal force against peaceful demonstrations, and arbitrarily detained and prosecuted activists, journalists, and political opposition members under martial law in North Kivu and Ituri.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed independent investigation with direct attribution to the martial-law governance structure under Tshisekedi.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because Tshisekedi's administration maintained the state of siege and set its duration.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes the government justified martial law as an anti-insecurity measure and the report is focused on abuse allegations.

evidence.claim: The AFP/Actualite report says Kabund was arrested in Kinshasa and charged with outrage against the head of state, harmful imputations, and defamation after he publicly denounced Tshisekedi's camp and launched his own party.
evidence.title: RDC: Kabund arrêté pour 'outrage au chef de l’État, imputations dommageables et diffamation'
evidence.excerpt: The AFP/Actualite report says Kabund was arrested in Kinshasa and charged with outrage against the head of state, harmful imputations, and defamation after he publicly denounced Tshisekedi's camp and launched his own party.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous wire-report corroboration with the charge language and political context spelled out.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Tshisekedi's political-space record.
contrary_evidence: The article also records criticism that the arrest could compromise free and credible 2023 elections.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri was being used to crush dissent, with two activists killed by security forces and dozens of critics arbitrarily detained on trumped-up charges.
evidence.title: DRC: One year on, 'State of Siege' used as a tool to crush dissent
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri was being used to crush dissent, with two activists killed by security forces and dozens of critics arbitrarily detained on trumped-up charges.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous briefing with named victims, dates, and a direct description of emergency-rule abuse.
evidence.period_fit: Within the 2022 target period; the state of siege began in 2021 but remained active throughout 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for the emergency regime; the abuses were carried out by security forces operating under a measure Tshisekedi kept in force and extended.
contrary_evidence: The government said the state of siege aimed to protect civilians from armed groups.
Armed-group violence also continued in the affected provinces.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi signed an ordinance changing the state-of-siege rules so military courts handled only specified grave offenses, reducing the prior transfer of civilian criminal jurisdiction to military courts.
evidence.title: RDC: Félix Tshisekedi modifie l’ordonnance sur l’état de siège et réduit les compétences pénales accordées aux juridictions militaires
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi signed an ordinance changing the state-of-siege rules so military courts handled only specified grave offenses, reducing the prior transfer of civilian criminal jurisdiction to military courts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a presidential ordinance with the text and stated government rationale summarized in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, and a partial corrective response to criticism of the original emergency regime.
contrary_evidence: The underlying state of siege remained in force.
The reform did not end the broader militarization of civilian justice.

evidence.claim: Al Jazeera reported that the May 2022 gubernatorial elections were tainted by irregularities, including allegations that candidates were bribed and provincial MPs were paid to vote in ways that favored the ruling coalition.
evidence.title: DR Congo: Provincial elections a dress rehearsal for 2023 polls
evidence.excerpt: Al Jazeera reported that the May 2022 gubernatorial elections were tainted by irregularities, including allegations that candidates were bribed and provincial MPs were paid to vote in ways that favored the ruling coalition.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with on-the-record civil-society and analyst allegations tied to a specific 2022 election process.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial but meaningful: the elections were run under Tshisekedi's presidency and the irregularities were attributed to the ruling coalition and its control over the process.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes some women were elected and that some seats were competitive.
It does not prove a direct presidential order for each alleged bribe.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi formally invested the three opposition delegates to the CENI after their approval by the National Assembly, completing the commission's membership.
evidence.title: RDC-CENI : Félix Tshisekedi a investi les trois membres de l'opposition
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi formally invested the three opposition delegates to the CENI after their approval by the National Assembly, completing the commission's membership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct reporting of a dated presidential act and the composition of the electoral commission.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action that included opposition representation, though the surrounding CENI design remained contested.
contrary_evidence: Opposition parties still disputed whether the CENI was genuinely independent.
The commission's broader composition remained politically contested.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi replaced the head of the armed forces as part of military reforms and that almost the entire staff was replaced by young officers, several from the Republican Guard.
evidence.title: Congo names new army chief among broad military reforms
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi replaced the head of the armed forces as part of military reforms and that almost the entire staff was replaced by young officers, several from the Republican Guard.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced report on concrete personnel changes and the government's own explanation of the reform.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment power, with some ambiguity because the government framed the change as reform for efficiency.
contrary_evidence: The government said the change aimed at boosting efficiency and military professionalism.
This is more about military control than civil political pluralism.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
